implementation_notes: kotlinx.coroutines' Channel is the idiomatic realization: send() suspends instead of blocking, receive() hands each element to exactly one receiver, and the documentation's fan-out section shows several receiving coroutines distributing the work of one channel - Competing Consumers in library form. Capacity is chosen at construction (rendezvous by default; BUFFERED/UNLIMITED/CONFLATED are the alternatives) and close() ends the stream in band while still delivering everything sent before it. JMS or Kafka via Java interop remains the choice when the channel must outlive the process.
code_sketch:
val jobs = Channel<Job>(capacity = 64)
repeat(4) { launch { for (job in jobs) handle(job) } }  // fan-out, one receiver each
for (j in batch) jobs.send(j)              // suspends when the buffer is full
jobs.close()                               // all queued jobs still delivered
pitfalls: consumeEach cancels the underlying channel when the coroutine completes (documented), so competing receivers must iterate with a plain for loop - consumeEach in fan-out kills the channel for the other workers.
A rendezvous (capacity 0) channel makes send() wait for a receiver; if all receivers are busy the producer stalls and the buffer you assumed is gone.
A Channel is in memory only: a process restart drops every buffered job, and JMS/Kafka interop is needed for durability.
